After two failed attempts in 1944, this Hindu nationalist activist shot Mahatma Gandhi three times at a Delhi prayer meeting in January 1948 — who was he?
Nathuram Godse: Assassin of Mahatma Gandhi (1910–1949)
This Imperial Japanese general captured Port Arthur twice — first from China in 1894, then from Russia a decade later — and became a national symbol of self-sacrificing loyalty — who is he?
Ruling Sweden and Norway from 1872, this monarch saw his joint crown split apart in 1905 when Norway's throne passed to a Danish prince — who was he?
Oscar II: King of Sweden (1872–1907) and Norway (1872–1905)
Fought from 431 to 404 BC, this clash between Athens's Delian League and Sparta's league turned only when Persia backed the Spartans — what conflict is it?
Peloponnesian War: War between Athens and Sparta (431–404 BC). The war consists of four related conflicts which have traditionally been combined into one.
Founded in 1967 by George Habash, this Marxist-Leninist faction pioneered airplane hijackings and remains the second-largest group within the PLO after Fatah. Which organization?
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine: Palestinian Marxist–Leninist organization. It has consistently been the second-largest of the groups forming the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), the largest being Fatah.
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Employed to paint glow-in-the-dark watch dials in the 1910s and 1920s, these American factory workers were told to point their brushes with their lips — ingesting a radioactive element that would reshape U.S. labor law. Who were they?
Radium Girls: American female radiation poisoning victims (1917–1978)
Known by the abbreviation PRO and led by former Argentine president Mauricio Macri, which party has governed Buenos Aires since 2007?
Republican Proposal: Political party in Argentina.
This granddaughter of a Michigan governor chaired the Republican National Committee from 2017 until resigning in 2024, presiding over a string of election losses — who is she?
A native of Zanzibar, she became Tanzania's first woman president in 2021 after ascending from the vice-presidency on her predecessor's death. Who is she?
Samia Suluhu Hassan: President of Tanzania since 2021. A native of Zanzibar, Suluhu served as a minister in the semi-autonomous region from 2000 to 2010.
Nicknamed "the Grim," this Ottoman sultan grew his empire by seventy percent in just eight years, conquering the entire Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt between 1516 and 1517 — who was he?
Selim I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1512 to 1520.
After a 1969 coup, this army commander became Somalia's third president and reconstituted the country as a one-party Marxist-Leninist state — who is he?
Siad Barre: President of Somalia from 1969 to 1991.
Based on the island of Sumatra, this maritime empire became a key center for spreading Buddhism across Southeast Asia between the 7th and 11th centuries — which empire?
Srivijaya: Empire based on Sumatra (c. 671–1025 AD)
Reigning nearly 48 years — the longest of any Tongan monarch — and standing 6 ft 3 in tall in her prime, this queen presided over what's called a golden age; who is she?
Sālote Tupou III: Queen of Tonga from 1918 to 1965.
Raised by his mother Aethra before discovering his royal father in Athens, this Greek hero is famed for slaying the Minotaur — who is he?
Theseus: Legendary king of Athens who slayed the Minotaur.

Walled off to the east and south by the Carpathians and to the west by the Apuseni Mountains, this historical region sits in central Romania and goes by Erdély in Hungarian and Siebenbürgen in German. What is it?
Transylvania: Historical region in Central Europe. Broader definitions of Transylvania also include the western and northwestern Romanian regions of Crișana and Maramureș, and occasionally Banat.
This Roman goddess of love and beauty was claimed as an ancestor by Julius Caesar through her son Aeneas, survivor of the fall of Troy?
Venus (mythology): Ancient Roman goddess of love, sex and fertility.
This Chinese diplomat served as ambassador to Japan before becoming Minister of Foreign Affairs and later director of the Communist Party's Central Foreign Affairs Commission Office — who is he?
Raised in Liverpool as the half-nephew of a Nazi dictator, this man later fought against his own uncle's regime in the US Navy — who is he, after changing his name postwar?
William Stuart-Houston: Half-nephew of Adolf Hitler (1911–1987)
A Hindu monk who became Uttar Pradesh's longest-serving and first two-term chief minister, he won five straight terms from Gorakhpur after entering parliament at just 26 — who is he?
Yogi Adityanath: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh since 2017.
Who wrote Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

Universal Declaration of Human Rights → United Nations General Assembly. All 193 member states of the UN have ratified at least one of the nine binding treaties influenced by the Declaration, with the vast majority ratifying four or more.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (born 1847) is the earliest of the four. Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 – March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Wallace Carothers is a chemist. Carothers was a group leader at the DuPont Experimental Station laboratory, near Wilmington, Delaware, where most polymer research was done.
What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron: Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Maria Montessori born?
Maria Montessori: At an early age, Montessori enrolled in classes at an all-boys technical school, with hopes of becoming an engineer.
In what year was Sundar Pichai born?
Sundar Pichai: Pichai began his career as a materials engineer.
In what year was Niels Bohr born?
Niels Bohr: Although the Bohr model has been supplanted by other models, its underlying principles remain valid.
In what year did Bernie Madoff die?
Bernie Madoff: Madoff's firm had two basic units: a stock brokerage and an asset management business; the Ponzi scheme was centered in the asset management business.
In what year did Louis Pasteur die?
Louis Pasteur: Pasteur's works are credited with saving millions of lives through the developments of vaccines for rabies and anthrax.
In what year was Fermat's Last Theorem discovered?
Fermat's Last Theorem: The proposition was first stated as a theorem by Pierre de Fermat around 1637 in the margin of a copy of Arithmetica.
In what year was Selenium discovered?
Selenium: Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
Metoprolol: Pfizer. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
In which country is Douglas A-4 Skyhawk based?
Douglas A-4 Skyhawk: United States. It was originally designated A4D under the United States Navy's pre-1962 designation system.
Who is credited with discovering Xenon?
Xenon: William Ramsay. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Who is credited with discovering RDX?
RDX: Georg Friedrich Henning. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Who is credited with discovering Aluminium?
Aluminium: Hans Christian Ørsted. Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
This tall wetland monocot, also known as muskrat root, may be toxic if ingested and has no proven clinical benefit despite traditional medicinal use — which plant?
Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.

This South African bulb genus tends to flower around March, earning a local nickname tied to that month, and is often confused with the Hippeastrum plants sold at Christmas under its common name — which genus?
Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
The largest genus in the arum family with roughly 1,000 species, this flowering plant group is native to the Americas, ranging from northern Mexico down to northern Argentina — which genus?
Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who was he?

Bernie Madoff (April 29, 1938 - April 14, 2021) was an American financier, con artist, and stock broker who was the admitted mastermind of the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion.
Accepted by the American Kennel Club in 1893, this small, compact dog breed with a short tail and erect ears originated in the United States — name the breed?
Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Sporting one pair of legs per body segment, this venomous arthropod always has an odd number of leg pairs — anywhere from 15 to 191 — what is it?

Centipede (from Neo-Latin centi- 'hundred' and Latin pes, pedis 'foot') are predatory arthropods belonging to the class Chilopoda of the subphylum Myriapoda, an arthropod group which includes millipedes and other multi-legged animals.
This small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa is often called a 'cat' in its common nickname, despite not actually being a cat at all — what is it?
Civet is a small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa, especially the tropical forests.

Forming colonies of thousands of genetically identical, sac-like polyps, these marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons behind the world's tropical reefs — name them?
Coral are colonial marine invertebrates within the subphylum Anthozoa of the phylum Cnidaria.
Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered photoelasticity and an angle that bears his name — and also improved the stereoscope. Who was he?
David Brewster (11 December 1781 - 10 February 1868) was a Scottish scientist, inventor, author, and academic administrator.
Charles Darwin spent years experimenting on these mucilage-coated plants, first proving that plants could be carnivorous — which genus of nearly 200 "sundew" species is it?
Drosera is commonly known as the sundews, is one of the largest genera of carnivorous plants, with at least 194 species.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.
What is the scientific term for the solid waste material left after digestion, discharged through the anus, and sometimes reused as fertilizer, fuel, or building material?
Feces (also faeces or fces or poop) are the solid or semi-solid remains of food that was not digested in the small intestine, and has been broken down by bacteria in the large intestine.
Alongside co-founding a file-sharing site, this Swedish entrepreneur also started an internet service provider and web-hosting firm called PRQ — who is he?
Fredrik Neij (born 27 April 1978), alias TiAMO, is the co-founder of The Pirate Bay, and the Swedish Internet service provider and web hosting company PRQ.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-molecular-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
Newborns with this severe genetic skin disorder are born encased in thick, diamond-shaped plates separated by deep cracks that restrict movement and breathing — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.
This American physicist threw out the wave-function collapse postulate, instead folding the observer into the same quantum state — an idea later known as the many-worlds interpretation. Who was he?
Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 - July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.
Patented in 1961 and approved two years later, this nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug works by blocking the enzyme cyclooxygenase to cut prostaglandin production — what drug is it?
Indometacin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used as a prescription medication to reduce fever, pain, stiffness, and swelling from inflammation.
Born in Albuquerque and a Princeton engineering graduate, this businessman founded and once ran Amazon, the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant — who is he?

Jeff Bezos (n Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company.
Also called a kilopond, this deprecated gravitational metric unit equals exactly 9.80665 newtons — the weight of a one-thousand-gram mass under standard gravity. What is it?
Kilogram-force (kgf or kgF), or kilopond (kp, from Latin pondus, 'weight'), is a non-standard gravitational metric unit of force equal to the weight on Earth of a one-kilogram mass.
This American computer scientist won the 2013 Turing Award for taming the chaos of distributed systems — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX — who is he?
Leslie Lamport (born February 7, 1941) is an American computer scientist and mathematician.
This SI unit quantifies the perceived power of visible light emitted by a source, weighted by how sensitive the human eye is to different wavelengths — what is it?
Lumen (unit) (symbol: lm) is the SI unit of luminous flux, which quantifies the perceived power of visible light emitted by a source.
This New Zealand actor currently plays a bar owner on the Netflix series Virgin River, and decades earlier starred in the horror remake The Ring. Who is he?
Marten is a weasel-like mammal in the genus Martes within the subfamily Guloninae, in the family Mustelidae.
This Hungarian-American psychologist identified and named the highly focused, creativity-boosting mental state known as 'flow' — who is he?
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi (29 September 1934 - 20 October 2021) was a Hungarian-American psychologist.
With somewhere between 66 and 70 species across nine subfamilies, this carnivore family stretches from tiny weasels all the way up to the wolverine. What is it?
Mustelidae (from Latin mustela, weasel) are a diverse family of carnivoran mammals, including weasels, badgers, otters, sea otters, polecats, martens, grisons and wolverines.
This American tech entrepreneur co-founded both Twitter and its predecessor podcasting company Odeo, and is credited with coining the name 'Twitter' itself — who is he?
Noah Glass is an American tech entrepreneur and software developer, who is known for co-founding the social media platform Twitter and Odeo, a podcasting company that shut down in 2017.
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
This chemical compound, known in nature as the mineral niter and historically as a form of saltpetre, is widely used in fertilizers. What is it?
Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
Powered by a supermassive black hole accreting gas at its center, this extremely luminous type of galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy thousands of times over. What is it?
Quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus (AGN).
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
With the formula AgNO3, this colorless, highly water-soluble compound is the least expensive salt of a lustrous precious metal and a precursor to many similar compounds — name it?
Silver nitrate is an inorganic compound with chemical formula AgNO3.
A self-taught Indian genius of infinite series and number theory, he initially struggled to interest established mathematicians because his methods were so unfamiliar — who was he?
Srinivasa Ramanujan (22 December 1887 - 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
This genus of coniferous evergreen in the cypress family includes five species — two native to North America, three to eastern Asia — and is sister to the genus Thujopsis. Name the genus?
Thuja is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
The most widespread New World scavenger of its kind, this bird sniffs out the gases of early decay to find carrion and rides thermals instead of flapping — which bird?
Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures.
What's the name for the small, non-cancerous skin growths caused by the human papillomavirus, most common on the hands and feet but also appearing as genital or filiform forms?
Wart are non-cancerous viral growths usually occurring on the hands and feet but which can also affect other locations, such as the genitals or face.
Atomic number 30, mined mostly from the ore sphalerite, this metal turns shiny blue-white once its surface oxidation is removed — which element?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.

First isolated from lymphoid tissue behind the nose in 1953, this family of nonenveloped DNA viruses ranges from causing the common cold to life-threatening illness in the immunocompromised — which family?
Sometimes called 'emotional blindness,' this condition makes it hard to identify or describe one's own feelings, and affects roughly half of people with autism. What is it?
Alexithymia: Deficiency in understanding, processing, or describing emotions.
Nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-flesh stench, this Sumatran plant first bloomed in cultivation at Kew Gardens in 1889 — which species?
Amorphophallus titanum: Species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.
This self-taught Dutch draper turned lensmaker began exploring microbial life with his own single-lensed microscopes in the 1670s, earning him the title 'Father of Microbiology' — who was he?
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?
Discovered by Robert Koch in 1876, this rod-shaped microbe was the first ever shown experimentally to cause disease, providing the earliest evidence for germ theory — which organism?
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who is it?
Bernie Madoff: American financier and con artist (1938–2021)

Developed to supplement the 727 on short routes, this narrow-body twinjet kept the 707's fuselage width and six-abreast seating and entered service with Lufthansa in 1968 — which best-selling aircraft is it?
A tree-like cluster of dark-green flower heads sprouting from a thick pale stalk, this cabbage-family vegetable is a close cousin of cauliflower and can be eaten raw or cooked — what is it?
Broccoli: Edible green plant in the cabbage family.
Named to honor the Virgin Mary and her golden crown, this daisy-family flower is also known as the pot marigold — which plant?
Calendula officinalis: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).
Often called 'the father of the computer,' this English polymath designed the difference engine and the analytical engine, borrowing a punch-card principle from the Jacquard loom — who is he?
Charles Babbage: English mathematician, philosopher, and engineer (1791–1871)
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on where you stand, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Americas — what is it?
Cougar: Wild cat species native to the Americas.
Native to Mexico and Central America, this tuberous flowering plant blooms in nearly every hue except blue, and its tubers store energy as inulin rather than starch — what is it?
Dahlia: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Historically defined by having two embryonic seed leaves, this once-standard division of flowering plants covers around 200,000 species but turned out not to share one common ancestor — which plant group?
Dicotyledon: Historical grouping of flowering plants.
One of the very first vertebrate apex predators on Earth, this armor-plated, jointed-neck fish patrolled open Devonian seas some 380 million years ago — which genus?
Born in Pretoria and once a Zip2 co-founder, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX became, by some estimates, the first dollar trillionaire in 2026 — who is he?
Elon Musk: Businessman and public official (born 1971)
Also called moral philosophy, this field splits into normative, applied, and meta- branches as it asks what people ought to do and whether objective moral facts even exist. Which discipline is it?
Proposed in 1724 by a physicist who set water's freezing point at 32 degrees and boiling at 212, this temperature scale was originally anchored to a freezing brine solution — which scale?
Fahrenheit: Temperature scale. The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale based on one proposed in 1724 by the physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit (1686–1736).
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?
Marketed as Neurontin, this anticonvulsant and GABA derivative is prescribed for nerve pain and partial seizures by binding to the α2δ subunits of calcium channels — what is it?
Endemic to China and sporting a handy 'thumb' on its forepaw to grip bamboo, this black-and-white bear weighs in around 100 to 115 kg — what animal is it?
Giant panda: Species of bear. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China.
Sporting pied black-and-white plumage with a red patch on its lower belly, this Palearctic bird drums on trees to mark territory and excavate nest holes — which species?
Great spotted woodpecker: Species of bird. The great spotted woodpecker (Dendrocopos major) is a medium-sized woodpecker with pied black and white plumage and a red patch on the lower belly.
Caused by mutations in the ABCA12 gene, this severe genetic skin disorder covers newborns in thick, cracked plates resembling armor — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis: Genetic skin disease. Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.
Traditionally drawn from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this blue compound is the color most associated with denim and blue jeans — what is it?
Indigo dye: Chemical compound, food additive and dye.
This American climatologist's 1988 Congressional testimony helped awaken the public to global warming, and he later turned activist — getting arrested more than once for the cause. Who is it?

Born John Chapman, this American pioneer nurseryman planted seed-grown apple trees across Pennsylvania, Ohio and beyond, becoming a folk hero in his own lifetime for his kindness and conservation. By what nickname do we know him?
A biologist and botanist married four times — her last husband directed the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos lab — she was played by Emily Blunt in a 2023 film. Who was she?
Spread through the bite of sandflies, this parasitic disease can appear in cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms, the last marked by fever and an enlarged spleen — what is it called?
Leishmaniasis: Disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type.

This catch-all name covers over 7,000 squamate species on every continent but Antarctica — from finger-length geckos to the three-meter Komodo dragon, with a few 'legless' lineages thrown in. What is it?
Found from Gibraltar to across Asia, these Old World monkeys live in troops centered on dominant matriarchs, and one Malaysian species eats about 70 rats a year — what are they?
Macaque: Genus of Old World monkeys. The macaques constitute a genus (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
Kangaroos, koalas, and wombats all belong to this mammal group whose young are born undeveloped and finish developing in their mother's pouch — what group is it?
Marsupial: Infraclass of mammals in the clade Metatheria.
The only operational rocket-powered fighter ever fielded, this WWII German interceptor became the first piloted aircraft to exceed 1,000 km/h in level flight — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet: German rocket-powered interceptor. The Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet is a rocket-powered interceptor aircraft primarily designed and produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Messerschmitt.
Named for the Latin for 'thousand feet,' no species of this many-legged arthropod class was confirmed to have 1,000-plus legs until a 2020 discovery with over 1,300 — what are they?
Millipede: Class of arthropods. Its primary defence mechanism is to curl into a tight coil, thereby protecting its legs and other vital delicate areas on the body behind a hard exoskeleton.
Named for a Tanzanian teenager who studied it scientifically in the 1960s, this puzzling phenomenon claims hot liquids can sometimes freeze faster than cold ones — what is it called?
Mpemba effect: Natural phenomenon that hot water freezes faster than cold.

Attributed to 19th-century pathologist Rudolf Virchow, this term for the premature death of cells caused by trauma or infection contrasts with the body's own programmed cell death — what's the condition called?
Necrosis: Unprogrammed cell death caused by external cell injury.
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
Mostly black on top, white below, and sporting unmistakable white eye patches, this cosmopolitan apex predator is actually the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family. What is it?
Orca: Largest living species of dolphin.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
As the only surviving son of a legendary Italian carmaker, this billionaire owns just over 10% of the company that bears his father's name and serves as its vice chairman — who is he?
Piero Ferrari: Italian billionaire businessman. Piero Ferrari (born Piero Lardi, 22 May 1945; later Piero Lardi Ferrari) is an Italian billionaire businessman and sport personality.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
This plant genus includes redcurrants, blackcurrants, and gooseberries, and also serves as the main alternate host for a fungal disease that attacks five-needle pines — which genus?
Ribes: Genus of flowering plants in the order Saxifragales.
